lines.trans: Let me show you to your suite.
Help me out, I urgently need a pianist for the evening.
Is this how you do not interfere in my personal life?

You went ahead and fired Denis yourself.

Misha, where is the pianist?
Which pianist?
The pianist whom Dima brought, find him.
I sent him to change clothes, an awful jacket.
Well you see, your Denis will be here.
You know very well that we broke up.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.trans: Let's go through the wedding script.

examples.text: Давайте я вам покажу ваш номер.
examples.trans: Let me show you to your suite.
Nikita, let's do it tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And you end up with six people.

examples.text: Вы у нас директор ресторана, Илья.
examples.trans: You are our restaurant director, Ilya.
And Dmitry Vladimirovich's tailcoat.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You tell me how to do it.

examples.text: Вы у нас директор ресторана, Илья.
examples.trans: You are our restaurant director, Ilya.
What are you doing here?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will show', paired with 'показывать'.

examples.trans: Show me your hands!
Shall we show this to Anikeev?

examples.text: Ну, покажите руки. Что у вас за спиной?
examples.trans: Well, show me your hands. What is behind your back?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Here, they brought your dress.
And your fingers too.

examples.text: Одно ваше присутствие — это уже подарок.
examples.trans: Your presence alone is already a gift.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'number' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Take it to my suite.
To make cookies from the family recipe.

examples.text: Давайте я вам покажу ваш номер.
examples.trans: Let me show you to your suite.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ручать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'help out'.

examples.text: Выручай, мне срочно нужен пианист на вечер.
examples.trans: Help me out, I urgently need a pianist for the evening.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и выручать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and help out on time.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Выручай, мне срочно нужен пианист на вечер.
examples.trans: Help me out, I urgently need a pianist for the evening.

examples.text: На кухне нужно срочно заменить холодильник.
examples.trans: In the kitchen we urgently need to replace the refrigerator.
Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('needed').

examples.trans: In short, what do you need?

examples.text: На кухне нужно срочно заменить холодильник.
examples.trans: In the kitchen we urgently need to replace the refrigerator.
I need a job too.

meanings.note: Agent noun formed with the international suffix '-ист' denoting a specialist or adherent. Common masculine noun meaning 'pianist' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Выручай, мне срочно нужен пианист на вечер.
examples.trans: Help me out, I urgently need a pianist for the evening.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: За нашим столиком будет сидеть олигарх.
examples.trans: An oligarch will be sitting at our table.

examples.trans: Wait, our table is for four.

examples.text: Вы у нас директор ресторана, Илья.
examples.trans: You are our restaurant director, Ilya.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Выручай, мне срочно нужен пианист на вечер.
examples.trans: Help me out, I urgently need a pianist for the evening.
Viktor Petrovich, good evening.
Good evening!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You tell me how to do it.

examples.text: И я хочу, чтобы повара испекли это печенье.
examples.trans: And I want the chefs to bake these cookies.

examples.text: Я читал сам про это дело.
examples.trans: I read about this matter myself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You cannot act like this.

examples.text: Я все-таки с острыми предметами работаю.
examples.trans: After all, I work with sharp objects.
And why is it so expensive?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не знаю, помнишь ты или нет.
examples.trans: I do not know whether you remember or not.
You are fired.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You tell me how to do it.
Take it to my suite.

examples.text: Я надеюсь, вам повторять не надо.
examples.trans: I hope I do not need to repeat to you.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'interfere', paired with 'вмешаться'.

examples.trans: And you, stay out of it.

examples.text: Подарки надо ценить! А вы не вмешивайтесь.
examples.trans: You must appreciate gifts! And you, stay out of it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They called and will definitely come.

examples.text: Подождите, у нас столик на четверых.
examples.trans: Wait, our table is for four.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh my goodness, thank you so much!
And where is my betrothed?

examples.text: Катя из-за тебя поговорила с мамой.
examples.trans: Katya talked to her mom because of you.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('personal').

examples.text: Это так ты не вмешиваешься в мою личную жизнь?
examples.trans: Is this how you do not interfere in my personal life?

examples.text: Сказала, не лезь в мою личную жизнь.
examples.trans: She said, do not meddle in my personal life.

examples.text: Я хочу предложить вам стать моим личным поваром.
examples.trans: I want to offer you to become my personal chef.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я виновата, я вмешивалась в твою жизнь.
examples.trans: I am at fault, I interfered in your life.

examples.text: Я никогда больше не буду лезть в твою жизнь.
examples.trans: I will never meddle in your life again.

examples.text: Это так ты не вмешиваешься в мою личную жизнь?
examples.trans: Is this how you do not interfere in my personal life?

meanings.en: to calm down, to settle down
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спокоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'calm down', paired with 'успокаиваться'.

examples.trans: Well, have you calmed down?
Calm down, please!
Calm down, everything's fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'myself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Извините, можно у вас автограф взять?

examples.text: Ты сама взяла и уволила Дениса.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'fired', paired with 'увольнять'.

examples.trans: Alright then, you fired everyone.

examples.text: Ты сама взяла и уволила Дениса.
examples.trans: You went ahead and fired Denis yourself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Извините, можно у вас автограф взять?
examples.trans: Excuse me, may I get your autograph?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'be'.

examples.trans: Maybe he left on his own?
I have a toy car.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They called and will definitely come.

examples.text: Замуж она выходит не в моем кабинете.
examples.trans: She is not getting married in my office.

examples.trans: Hello, glad to see you.

examples.trans: Where is Louis?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('what').

examples.trans: You tell me how to do it.

examples.text: У вас ко мне какое-то дело?
examples.trans: Do you have some business with me?

examples.text: Пианист, которого Дима привел, найди его.
examples.trans: The pianist whom Dima brought, find him.
This is a mayor who keeps his word.
Where is the book that was here?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'вести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring, to lead (someone somewhere)', paired with 'приводить'.

examples.trans: Bring him tomorrow to the hospital.
The father brought his son to the doctor.
You will bring the child in the morning.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Пианист, которого Дима привел, найди его.
examples.trans: The pianist whom Dima brought, find him.
Where will I find movers?
I found the phone.

meanings.en: to send (a person, a letter, a message)
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'править'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'sent', paired with 'отправлять'.

examples.text: Я его отправил переодеваться, ужасный пиджак.
examples.trans: I sent him to change clothes, an awful jacket.
I sent the letter.
Send me a message.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'одеваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to get changed, change clothes', paired with 'переодеться'.

examples.text: Я его отправил переодеваться, ужасный пиджак.
examples.trans: I sent him to change clothes, an awful jacket.
He changes into uniform.
And you, go get changed!

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'жасный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('terrible').

examples.text: Я его отправил переодеваться, ужасный пиджак.
examples.trans: I sent him to change clothes, an awful jacket.
What a horrible person you are!
It's a terrible flat.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'suit jacket' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я его отправил переодеваться, ужасный пиджак.
examples.trans: I sent him to change clothes, an awful jacket.

examples.text: Тот странный мужчина в тёмном пиджаке.
examples.trans: That strange man in the dark jacket.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: In short, what do you need?
Unbelievable, ten million for infidelity.
Alright then, you fired everyone.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: Did you want to see me?

How glad I am to see you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я виновата, я вмешивалась в твою жизнь.
examples.trans: I am at fault, I interfered in your life.

examples.text: Я никогда больше не буду лезть в твою жизнь.
examples.trans: I will never meddle in your life again.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ты прекрасно знаешь, что мы расстались.
examples.trans: You know very well that we broke up.
I understand perfectly.
Wonderful! Thank you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'know'.

examples.text: Не знаю, помнишь ты или нет.
examples.trans: I do not know whether you remember or not.

examples.text: Ты прекрасно знаешь, что мы расстались.
examples.trans: You know very well that we broke up.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Eleonora Andreyevna, sorry to interrupt.
Why are we standing around?
What are you doing here?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты прекрасно знаешь, что мы расстались.
examples.trans: You know very well that we broke up.

examples.text: Мы ведь в ЗАГС так можем опоздать.
examples.trans: We might be late to the registry office like this.
What do you mean?

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'статься'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'broke up, separated', paired with 'расставаться'.

examples.trans: We will definitely break up.
They broke up last summer.

examples.text: Нет, я всё решил! Мы с ней точно расстанемся.
examples.trans: No, I have decided everything! She and I will definitely break up.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нципиальный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('matter-of-principle').

examples.trans: This is a matter of principle.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень принципиальный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very matter-of-principle choice.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'прос'). Common masculine noun meaning 'question' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a matter of principle.
I have a question.
It's a very important matter.
